question: Does the trained hidden block provide feature efficiency beyond equally budgeted untrained nonlinear maps of full input?

design.question: Does the trained hidden block provide feature efficiency beyond equally budgeted untrained nonlinear maps of full input?
design.evidence: Post-hoc exploratory predictive follow-up on the already evaluated64-source cohort. Historical results cannot be made unseen by freezing this new analysis. No new native inference or new information beyond deterministic input transforms is claimed.
design.fit: Exactly oldFIT20 source groups/96 rows. Same4 source-grouped folds, source weights, stable tie rule and FIT-only preprocessing as trained extension. No fresh64 target enters selection.

maps.input: All128 normalized history values plus history mean/SD and logSD;130 values recover full physical history. FIT-only coordinate standardization of input axes.
maps.rff: D cosine features, Gaussian projection variance2/FIT median squared distance (fixed gamma1), random uniform phase, sqrt(2/D) amplitude.
maps.mlp_relu: One untrained affine/ReLU hidden layer of widthD, Gaussian He weights and N(0,1) biases. No learned map weights or nonlinear-family tuning.

budget.scope: Matches flattened feature width, supervised readout rank/grid/folds/labels; does NOT match pretrained network architecture, parameter count, inference FLOPs or pretraining compute.

design.base: Freeze original input+Aforecast kernel separately for each target; retain its input and Aforecast blocks. Replace added trained-hidden kernel by random-feature PCA kernel. All3 blocks equal weight1/3. Random PCA rank/alpha selected per family/init using only oldFIT, same8 choices as trained extension.
design.report: Report every initialization, no best seed or family. For each of2 families x3 targets, average squared loss across the3 fixed initializations (NOT prediction ensembling), then average cases within source. Report random-minus-trained loss and gain over input+Aforecast, paired source bootstrap4000 draws. Six trained-advantage intervals use99.16666666666667% coverage; individual-init intervals95%, all exploratory.
design.interpretation: A trained advantage is conditional feature/readout efficiency under these recipes, not information-theoretic independence, causality or semantic equivalence. Random competitiveness is counterevidence to uniqueness; failure to reject difference is not equivalence.

next_decision: Keep native HOLD. Review a limited new-condition study focused on fusion-response efficiency, with frozen-transfer and matched local-FIT axes, forecast targets as controls, and no pooled natural-data claim.

events.next_decision: Cached TEST evaluation permitted; native remains HOLD.

interpretation.counterevidence: Generic untrained nonlinear features reproduce or exceed forecast-emulation gains. There is no broad trained-hidden advantage across these two families.
interpretation.bounded_support: Trained TimesFM hidden retains a fusion-response prediction advantage over both random families under matched readout budgets; about7.7% lower loss.
interpretation.information_statement: Deterministic hidden features introduce no information beyond the complete input. These comparisons measure supervised finite-budget feature/readout efficiency.
interpretation.scope: Previously inspected synthetic TEST cohort; no causal, equivalent-semantic, universal-random-family or natural-data claim.
